scope: Manual device-local Windows game registry, on-open detection and explicit opt-in background detection; not complete global game activity or overlay.
implementation: A separate cross-platform-visible Registered Games settings page uses verified additive IPC. Native file selection registers eligible existing executable files locally; missing/unreadable selections reject with path-free errors. Deleted registered files remain visible with unknown running state and recovery guidance.

A fixed bounded Windows PowerShell/CIM query receives known image names as data through stdin, not interpolated command text. Matching uses canonical case-insensitive executable paths, not basename alone; protected null paths remain unknown. Only matching results remain in main; no full process inventory or absolute path is returned to the renderer or server.

Registry reads and writes have byte/schema/count bounds, serialized mutations and failure rollback. Corruption or permission errors do not overwrite saved registrations. The settings page polls while open; stale polls cannot resurrect removed entries. Current/recent sections use real local detection timestamps and the global time formatter.

A separate device-local backgroundDetectionEnabled consent defaults false, is stored additively in the existing v1 registry, and restores on app start. When explicitly enabled, main checks registered executables every 30 seconds independently of settings mounting. Foreground/background requests share one scan; interval ticks cannot queue a backlog. Disabling or quitting invalidates queued background generations before native scan and before last-seen commit; dispose prevents further scans. Running applications are not a foreground/play-duration assertion.

Per-game local sharing consent defaults off, persists locally and is explicitly described as not yet connected to server activity. No verified-game badge, external catalog attribution, automatic discovery catalog or join adapter is invented.
